The Petitioner-accused No.1 who is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under sections 354, 323, 504, 506 r/w Section 34 of IPC, is before this Court.
2. Cognizance taken of the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
4. Respondent No.2 had lodged FIR in Crime No.142/2016 registered by the Ramamurthynagar Police station for the offence punishable under Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961,
Section 34 of IPC, Section 3(1) (10) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and section 498A of IPC.
5.

sentences.text: In the said FIR among other allegation it was alleged that, on 6.3.2021 when she went to speak to her husband, at that time, the petitioner-accused No.1 pulled her husband and locked him in a room and thereafter snatched her NC: 2023:KHC:28807 car key, mobile and purse and after locking the door of the house manhandled and threatened her with life and also threatened that he would not allow her to lead a marital life with her husband.
6. The Police after investigation submitted the 'B' report with the jurisdictional Magistrate, and the 2nd respondent filed a protest petition to the said 'B' report.

Pending enquiry of the same, the 2nd respondent lodged 2nd FIR making similar allegation with regard to the incident i.e., alleged to have taken place on 6.3.2016 which was the subject matter of the Crime No.142/2016 and the incident that took place on 6.3.2016 was already investigated by the Police and the Police

sentences.text: 7. It is also pointed out that the learned Magistrate after recording the sworn statement of the 2nd respondent has rejected the protest petition and accepted the 'B' report submitted by the Police.

Hence, the registration of the 2nd FIR on the very same incident is an abuse of process of law and violates Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
8.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Amitbhai Anil Chandra Shah v. CBI and Anr (2013) 6 SCC 348 para 58.5 has held as follows:
"58.5.

entities.text: Amitbhai Anil Chandra Shah v. CBI and Anr (2013) 6 SCC 348
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The first information report is a report which gives first information with regard to any offence.

There cannot be second FIR in respect of the same offence/event NC: 2023:KHC:28807 because whenever any further information is received by the investigating agency, it is always in furtherance of the first FIR."
9.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Petition is allowed;
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.257/2019 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge & CJM Chikkaballapura, insofar it relates to the petitioner-accused No.1 herein stands quashed.
Sd/-
